languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_switchNotebook
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists all open Wolfram notebooks or switches the active editor to a specific one. Use action='list' (default) to see all open .wb notebooks with their cell counts and active status — call this first when you need to work with a different notebook. Use action='switch' with a notebook filename (e.g. 'test.wb') to bring that notebook to the foreground and make it the target for all subsequent tool calls. After switching, tools like wolfbook_getNotebookContext, wolfbook_insertCell, wolfbook_runCell etc. will operate on the newly activated notebook. You can also pass the optional 'notebook' parameter directly to wolfbook_getNotebookContext to read a specific notebook without switching the active editor.

action.description: 'list' (default) to show all open notebooks; 'switch' to bring a specific notebook to the foreground.

notebook.description: Filename of the notebook to switch to (e.g. 'test.wb'). Required when action='switch'.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_getNotebookContext
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns a structured text representation of the currently open Wolfram Language notebook (or a specific notebook if the optional 'notebook' parameter is provided). Includes all cell sources (code and markdown), section headings, and cell outputs as LaTeX. Use this before writing or editing Wolfram Language code to understand what symbols are already defined, what has been computed, and what the mathematical goal of the notebook is. Pass notebook='filename.wb' to read a different open notebook without switching the active editor. Use startCell/endCell to read only a range of cells instead of the entire notebook — useful for large notebooks when you know which cells you need.

notebook.description: Optional: filename of a specific open notebook to read (e.g. 'prototype.wb'). If omitted, reads the currently active notebook.

startCell.description: Optional: 1-based cell number to start reading from. Defaults to 1 (beginning of notebook). Use with endCell to read a specific range.

endCell.description: Optional: 1-based cell number to end at (inclusive). Defaults to the last cell. Use with startCell to read a specific range.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_evaluateExpression
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Evaluates a Wolfram Language expression in the active notebook's live kernel and returns the result as InputForm text. CRITICAL — multi-expression pitfall: passing multiple lines WITHOUT semicolons in single-expression mode (multiLine:false) causes the kernel to interpret newline-separated subexpressions as Times[...] multiplication, NOT as sequential statements — always use explicit semicolons (;) between statements, or set multiLine:true. Set multiLine:true to evaluate each non-empty line as a separate, independent expression — results are labeled Out[1]=, Out[2]=, etc.; lines ending with ; are evaluated silently. State accumulates across lines. Do not use for long-running computations.

expression.description: A valid Wolfram Language expression to evaluate.

timeoutSeconds.description: Maximum seconds to wait for result (default: 10).

multiLine.description: If true, the expression is split on newlines (\n) and each non-empty line is evaluated as a SEPARATE, COMPLETE Wolfram Language expression — exactly like pressing Shift+Enter on each line one by one. Results are returned labeled Out[1]=, Out[2]=, etc. Lines ending with ; are evaluated silently (output suppressed). State accumulates across lines. IMPORTANT: each line must be a syntactically complete WL expression on its own (e.g. "f[x_] := x^2" on one line). Multi-line WL constructs must be collapsed to a single line before passing. The separator is always \n (newline character); do NOT use semicolons as the line separator — use ; only to suppress output within a single expression.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_evaluateAndInsert
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Evaluates a Wolfram Language expression in the live kernel: if the evaluation is clean (no kernel error messages, or the output matches the optional expectedOutput string), the expression is inserted as a new code cell in the notebook. Returns the evaluation result plus either an insert confirmation or an explanation of why it was not inserted. Use this to reduce the two-step workflow of: evaluate-to-test → manually insert the same code. Typical use: write a definition, verify it raises no errors, and land it in the notebook in one tool call. If expectedOutput is given, insertion only happens when the result string starts with that value (e.g. pass '0' to require a zero residual). Position defaults to 'end'; pass a cell number or 'after-cursor' to control placement.

expression.description: A valid Wolfram Language expression to evaluate and (if clean) insert as a new code cell.

expectedOutput.description: Optional. If given, the cell is only inserted when the evaluation result string starts with this value (e.g. '0', 'True', 'Null'). If omitted, insertion proceeds as long as there are no kernel error messages.

position.description: Where to insert the new cell (same semantics as wolfbook_insertCell). Defaults to 'end'.

timeoutSeconds.description: Maximum seconds to wait for the evaluation (default: 15).

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_lookupSymbol
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns the usage message and definition for a Wolfram Language symbol. Use this when unsure about the syntax or behaviour of a built-in function, or to understand a user-defined function in the notebook before using it.

symbol.description: The name of the Wolfram Language symbol to look up (e.g. 'BBrel', 'Solve', 'Signature').

longForm.description: If true (default), appends a clickable link to the online Wolfram documentation page at the bottom of the result. Only applies to built-in System-context symbols.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_getSymbolWebHelp
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Fetches the full online Wolfram Language documentation page for a built-in symbol from reference.wolfram.com and returns its text content. Use this when you need detailed examples, complete option descriptions, or behaviour details beyond what wolfbook_lookupSymbol provides. Only works for System-context (built-in) symbols.

symbol.description: The name of the Wolfram Language built-in symbol (e.g. 'FindRoot', 'NIntegrate', 'Plot').

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_insertCell
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Inserts a new code or markdown cell into the active Wolfram notebook at a specified position. Call wolfbook_getNotebookContext first to see Cell numbers. Set evaluate: true on code cells to also run the cell in the live kernel immediately after inserting — the result is returned alongside the insert confirmation, so you can verify the output without a second tool call. position: 'end' appends, 'after-cursor' inserts after the selected cell, or a number N inserts after Cell N from wolfbook_getNotebookContext (0 = before Cell 1).

position.description: Where to insert: a number N inserts after Cell N (use Cell numbers from wolfbook_getNotebookContext; 0 = before Cell 1), 'after-cursor' inserts after the currently selected cell, or 'end' appends at the end.

kind.description: Cell type: 'code' for Wolfram Language expressions that will be sent to the kernel for evaluation; 'markdown' for explanatory text, headings, or LaTeX math — markdown cells are never evaluated by the kernel.

evaluate.description: If true (and kind is "code"), evaluate the cell content in the live kernel immediately after inserting it and include the result in the response. Requires the kernel to be running and idle.

timeoutSeconds.description: Maximum seconds to wait for the evaluation result when evaluate: true (default: 15).

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_insertCells
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Inserts a contiguous block of new cells into the active Wolfram notebook in a single operation. Prefer this over multiple wolfbook_insertCell calls whenever you need to add 2 or more cells. Call wolfbook_getNotebookContext first to get current cell numbers. position=N inserts after Cell N (0 = before Cell 1); 'end' appends; 'after-cursor' inserts after the selected cell. Each cell in the cells array specifies kind ('code' for Wolfram Language or 'markdown' for text/headings/LaTeX) and content.

position.description: Where to insert the block: a number N inserts after Cell N (use Cell numbers from wolfbook_getNotebookContext; 0 = before Cell 1), 'end' appends at the end, or 'after-cursor' inserts after the currently selected cell.

cells.description: Ordered list of cells to insert as a contiguous block.

kind.description: Cell type: 'code' for Wolfram Language expressions that will be sent to the kernel for evaluation; 'markdown' for explanatory text, headings, or LaTeX math — markdown cells are never evaluated by the kernel.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_deleteCell
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Deletes one or more cells from the active Wolfram notebook. Deleted content is saved to ai_deleted_cells.md for recovery (use wolfbook_restoreDeletedCells to undo). Call wolfbook_getNotebookContext first to confirm cell numbers. Pass cellNumber for a single cell or cellNumbers (array) for multiple — they are removed in descending index order so earlier indices remain accurate. Each deleted cell's content is returned as confirmation.

cellNumber.description: 1-based cell number to delete (single cell). Use cellNumbers for multiple.

cellNumbers.description: Array of 1-based cell numbers to delete (multiple cells). Cells are deleted in descending index order.

saveToRecovery.description: If true (default), save deleted cell content to ai_deleted_cells.md before removing.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_restoreDeletedCells
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists or restores recently deleted cells from the ai_deleted_cells.md recovery log maintained by wolfbook_deleteCell. Use action="list" to browse the last N deleted cells (default 10) — useful to review what was just removed or to confirm what to restore. Use action="restore" to re-insert the last N deleted cells at a specified position (default: end of notebook). The recovery log is never cleared.

action.description: "list" to show recent deleted cells; "restore" to re-insert them into the notebook.

count.description: How many recent deletions to list or restore (default: 10 for list, 1 for restore).

insertPosition.description: Where to insert restored cells: "end" (default) or a 1-based cell index N (inserts before Cell N).

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_moveCell
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Moves a cell from one position to another within the active Wolfram notebook. Reordering is done atomically (delete + re-insert in one edit), so notebook cell numbers shift as expected. Call wolfbook_getNotebookContext first to confirm cell numbers. Use toPosition=0 to move a cell to the very beginning, or toPosition=N to place it after Cell N.

cellNumber.description: 1-based number of the cell to move.

toPosition.description: Insert the cell after this 1-based cell number. Use 0 to move it to the very beginning (before Cell 1).

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_runAllCells
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Executes a range of cells in the active Wolfram notebook sequentially — one at a time, waiting for each to finish before starting the next. Returns a per-cell summary of status and text/plain output. Useful for clean-run validation after a kernel restart or after editing many cells. Markdown cells are automatically skipped. Set stopOnError:true to halt on the first kernel message/error.

startCell.description: 1-based cell number to start from (default: 1 = beginning of notebook).

endCell.description: 1-based cell number to end at, inclusive (default: last cell).

timeoutSeconds.description: Total time budget for the entire run in seconds (default: 120). Individual cells are each capped at 5 minutes or the remaining budget, whichever is smaller.

stopOnError.description: If true, stop the run when a cell produces a kernel message/error (default: false — run all cells regardless).

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_findPackage
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Searches for Wolfram Language packages on the Wolfram Paclet Server (via PacletFindRemote) and on GitHub. Returns names, descriptions, and ready-to-run install commands for each result. For Paclet Server hits the result includes the exact PacletInstall["Name"] command; for GitHub hits it includes the releases URL and explains both the .paclet-URL install path and the URLDownload+ExtractArchive+AppendTo[$Path]+Get workflow for plain source repos. After finding a package, use wolfbook_evaluateExpression with timeoutSeconds>=120 to run the install command — do NOT guess install syntax, always use the commands returned by this tool.

query.description: Search term, e.g. "numerical ODE", "quantum field theory", "cluster algebra". Alphanumeric words and hyphens only.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_kernelCrashLog
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Reads the Wolfram kernel debug log (img/<notebookName>/wolfram-kernel-debug.log) and/or macOS crash reports (~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/) to help diagnose kernel crashes and unexpected disconnections. The debug log lives next to btl.log in the notebook's img/ subfolder and is recreated fresh each kernel start. Crash reports contain stack traces from kernel aborts. Use source="debug" for the live debug log, source="crash" for crash reports, source="all" for both.

source.description: "debug" (default) reads the kernel debug log from img/<notebookName>/; "crash" reads macOS DiagnosticReports; "all" reads both.

lines.description: How many tail lines of the debug log to return (default: 150, max: 1000).

filter.description: Optional keyword or regex to filter log lines (case-insensitive). E.g. "ERROR", "ABORT", "crash".

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_editCell
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Replaces the source code of an existing cell in the active Wolfram notebook. Use this to fix bugs, update expressions, or refine output formatting in cells that have already been inserted. Call wolfbook_getNotebookContext first to confirm cell numbers and current source. Set evaluate:true to immediately run the updated content in the kernel and confirm the result. IMPORTANT: the content string must be syntactically correct Wolfram Language exactly as it should appear in the cell. Do NOT add extra blank lines between statements just to look pretty — write multi-statement code as a compact block.

content.description: The new source text for the cell. Write it exactly as it should appear in the cell — do NOT add extra blank lines between statements to format it nicely, as this creates invalid syntax for single-expression inputs. Multi-line constructs like Module[...] are fine as long as brackets match.

evaluate.description: If true (and the cell is a code cell), evaluate the new content in the live kernel immediately after editing and include the result in the response.

timeoutSeconds.description: Maximum seconds to wait for evaluation when evaluate:true (default: 15).

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_runCell
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Executes an existing notebook cell through the normal Wolfbook execution pipeline (equivalent to pressing Shift+Enter), waits for completion, and returns the cell output summary. Unlike wolfbook_evaluateExpression, the result is stored as the cell output in the notebook and visible to the user. Output format: first line is 'Cell N of M executed (T s).' followed by the result text, or '(no output — definition or suppressed expression)' when the cell defines functions or uses trailing semicolons. If the kernel emitted messages or errors they are appended as '⚠ Kernel messages (N):' — treat any such messages as errors that need fixing. Use wolfbook_getNotebookContext to read back the cell output in detail if needed.

timeoutSeconds.description: Maximum seconds to wait for the execution to finish (default: 30).

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_getKernelState
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns a summary of the current Wolfram kernel state: all user-defined symbols matching a context pattern, showing their values (for direct assignments) or rule counts (for functions with DownValues). Default pattern 'Global`*' shows everything defined interactively. Use a narrower pattern like 'QSC`*' to inspect a specific package context. Call this before inserting or editing code to understand what is already defined and avoid naming conflicts.

pattern.description: Wolfram context pattern to match symbols against (default: 'Global`*'). Examples: 'Global`*', 'QSC`*', 'Global`Q*'.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_saveNotebook
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Saves the active Wolfram notebook to disk. Call this after a batch of cell insertions, edits, or deletions to persist the changes. The file is saved to its current path — no dialog is shown and the user does not need to intervene.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_restartKernel
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Restarts the Wolfram kernel. All in-memory definitions and variable values are lost; rendered cell outputs are preserved. Use this when the kernel is stuck, has crashed, or the user asks for a fresh kernel state. The user will be shown a confirmation dialog before the restart proceeds.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_abortEvaluation
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Sends an abort signal to the Wolfram kernel to interrupt the currently running evaluation. Use this when an evaluation is taking too long, is stuck in an infinite loop, or the user asks to stop the computation. Has no effect if no evaluation is currently running.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_debugCell
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Controls the Wolfbook step-through debugger. Use action="analyze" to inspect a cell's step structure before debugging. Use action="start" to begin a debug session on a cell (kernel pauses at first step). Use action="status" to check if a session is active and see the last known step info. Use action="stepOver" to execute the current statement and pause at the next one at the same or outer loop level. Use action="stepInto" to enter an inner loop body (pauses at first statement inside). Use action="stepOut" to finish the current loop level and return to the parent. Use action="continue" to run until the next breakpoint. Use action="runToEnd" to run the cell to completion ignoring breakpoints. Use action="stop" to abort the debug session. All step/continue/stop commands require an active session (check with action="status"). Timings are recorded automatically and shown as inline annotations after each session. Use action="addBreakpoint" with a "line" number (1-based) and optional "cellNumber" to set a breakpoint; use action="removeBreakpoint" similarly to remove one; action="clearBreakpoints" removes all (or all for a specific cell if cellNumber is given); action="listBreakpoints" shows all current breakpoints. Use action="addWatch" with "variableName" to add a variable to the Watch Panel; action="removeWatch" to remove one; action="listWatch" to see the current watch list.

action.description: The operation to perform. Use analyze or start before session; use step/continue/stop while paused; use addBreakpoint/removeBreakpoint/clearBreakpoints/listBreakpoints for breakpoint management; use addWatch/removeWatch/listWatch for the Watch Panel variable list.

cellNumber.description: 1-based cell number for action=analyze, action=start, action=addBreakpoint, action=removeBreakpoint, or action=clearBreakpoints. Omit to use the currently selected cell.

line.description: 1-based line number within the cell. Required for action=addBreakpoint and action=removeBreakpoint.

variableName.description: Wolfram Language variable name for action=addWatch or action=removeWatch.

showInstrumentedCode.description: For action=analyze: if true (default), include the full instrumented code in the result.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_searchCells
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Searches notebook cells for a given query string or regex pattern. Returns matching cell numbers with source previews and whether the match was in the source code, output, or both. Use this to quickly locate cells containing a specific variable, function, or error message without reading the entire notebook. Useful in long notebooks before calling wolfbook_getNotebookContext with a targeted startCell/endCell range.

query.description: The text or regex pattern to search for (case-insensitive).

regex.description: If true, treat query as a regular expression. Default: false (plain text search).

kind.description: Optional: restrict search to only code or only markdown cells.

includeOutput.description: If true (default), also search cell outputs, not just source code.

languageModelTools.name: wolfteam_proposePlan
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Call this tool when you have formulated a multi-step calculation plan and need the user to approve it before you begin executing. Pass the plan summary and list of steps. The user will see the plan in a confirmation dialog and click Allow to approve, or Deny to reject. Do NOT execute any steps until this tool returns successfully.

planSummary.description: One-paragraph summary of what the plan will accomplish

steps.description: Ordered list of steps to execute

languageModelTools.name: wolfteam_askDecision
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Call this tool when you reach a conceptual decision point — a choice of gauge, coordinate system, ansatz, expansion strategy, or any fork where the user's physics expertise should guide the direction. Present the question, the available options, and a default. The user can edit the selectedOption parameter before approving. Do NOT guess — always call this tool at genuine decision points.

selectedOption.description: The user's selected option — user can edit this before clicking Allow

context.description: Brief context for why this decision matters

languageModelTools.name: wolfteam_checkpoint
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Call this tool after completing a significant calculation step to show the user the intermediate result and what comes next. The user clicks Allow to continue or Deny to pause and inspect. Use between major steps, not after every trivial evaluation.

result.description: The key result or output (keep concise)

nextStep.description: What will be done next if user approves
